sentences.text:
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Sunil is in judicial custody in Fir No.164 of 2023 (In Bail Application No.45 of 2024),
under Sections 420 and 120B Ipc, Police Station Gadarpur, District Udham Singh Nagar.

He has
sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3. It is a case of online fraud.
According to the informant, on 02.06.2023, somebody called him introducing himself as the son of the friend of the informant and demanded money.
As indicated by the caller, according to the FIR, the informant transmitted Rs.7,66,000/- in different accounts.
Out of which, Rs.50,000/- was sent to the applicant through UPI.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that there is no KYC.
Sunil, who is named in the FIR, is not the applicant.
The FIR is delayed by 47 days which was lodged on 19.07.2023.

Therefore,
it is a case fit for bail.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the applicant is the same Sunil whom the applicant transferred Rs.50,000/- through UPI based on the instructions of the caller.
He would refer Annexure-1 to the counter affidavit at serial no.6, which reveals that Rs.50,000/- was transmitted in the account of the applicant.
The name, address, residence is one of the same.
He would also refer to the bank statement.
6. Learned State Counsel would also submit that the telephone alert was also sent on the mobile number of the applicant.
7. It is the stage of bail.
Much of the discussion at this stage is not expected of.

To the extent of appreciating the controversy, the matter may be examined with the caveat that any observation,

sentences.text: 8. In such cases, to collect the evidence is one of the little tough task.
In the instant case, the FIR records that the informant was cheated to the tune of Rs. Rs.7,66,000/-.

Out of which, Rs.50,000/-
was deposited through UPI.
Now, the bank details submitted by the prosecution reveals that it is the applicant, in whose account, Rs.50,000/- was deposited on the date of incident.
The telephone alert reached to the applicant's mobile number.
9. Having considered, this Court is of the view that there is no ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The bail application deserves to be rejected.
10. The bail application is rejected.
